statements.venue: House Homeland Security subcommittee hearing, opening statement
statements.quote: Further reporting suggested that DeepSeek employees used third-party routers and networks of unauthorized resellers to circumvent existing safeguards, and may have sought to override safety protections around biological and chemical weapons research.
statements.context: Hearing on threats from Chinese AI, robotics and autonomous technologies; the statement is about DeepSeek's alleged theft of American models, data going to China, and vulnerabilities in Unitree robots.
statements.source_label: House Homeland Security Committee (Republican) press release, 17 March 2026
statements.reason: The statement is about competition with China, theft and data security; it relays reporting about a Chinese firm bypassing weapons-related safety protections but does not itself name a catastrophic harm from AI, so D (close to C misuse_only).

record: Sponsored H.R. 5351, the National Science Foundation Artificial Intelligence Education Act of 2025, on AI education and workforce.
grade_reason: He has spoken about AI in 2025 and 2026 (education, competition with China, Chinese AI and robot security), but nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk from AI.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. The searches on AI safety, superintelligence, extinction, pause and China agreement returned nothing about him. No source shows him as a cosponsor of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced by Rep. Casar on 24 September 2026); the cosponsors named in reports are Democrats, but I did not open the full congress.gov cosponsor list. The 17 March 2026 hearing statement mentions DeepSeek possibly overriding safety protections around biological and chemical weapons research; a reviewer may judge this C with misuse_only, but it is framed as reporting about a Chinese company and the harms he stresses are theft, data and economic or military advantage, so I labelled it D with boundary. The hearing statement was published on the Homeland Security Committee's site, not fong.house.gov.
